shared_elements: upright monolithic stone block as the carrying surface
low-relief carving raised slightly from a flat stone face
one element rendered in higher, more rounded relief against flatter surrounding carving
a hand/limb motif on the stone's face
large plain uncarved area of stone below the carved zone
justification: Both are tall, roughly rectangular stone monoliths whose relief decoration (including a hand-like appendage and rounded raised bosses) sits on the upper part of a vertical face while the lower stone is left comparatively plain, which is the most specific correspondence. Otherwise they differ sharply: A is a dark, densely covered figure with a broad headdress-like top, banded torso and large disc, whereas B is a pale, sparsely carved pillar bearing a single high-relief animal-like creature and an incised arm, set in a rubble wall, so the density, palette and carving manner have little in common.
